questions.statement: Which structure expresses a future plan?
questions.context: In a classroom in Tunja, Boyacá, the teacher explains how to talk about plans for Saturday.

options.text: I am going to visit my grandmother.
options.feedback: Correct: be + going to + verb expresses a future plan.

options.text: I visit my grandmother every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect: that is a present routine, not a future plan.

options.text: I visited my grandmother yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect: that is past, not a future plan.

options.text: I visiting my grandmother now.
options.feedback: Incorrect: that is incomplete and points to the present, not the future.

questions.explanation: Going to sirve para hablar de planes futuros: se forma con el verbo be (am/is/are) + going to + verbo principal.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word names a place to watch movies?
questions.context: In Pasto, Nariño, a poster lists weekend places: park, cinema, library and stadium.

options.text: Park.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the park is for games and walks, not movies.

options.text: Library.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the library is for reading and borrowing books.

options.text: Cinema.
options.feedback: Correct: the cinema is the place where people watch movies.

options.text: Bakery.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the bakery sells bread, it does not show movies.

questions.explanation: El vocabulario de lugares del fin de semana incluye cinema (cine), park (parque), library (biblioteca) y stadium (estadio).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Neiva, Huila, Camilo tells his friend about Saturday: "I ___ play football in the stadium". He needs am/is/are.

options.text: I is going to play football in the stadium.
options.feedback: Incorrect: is goes with he/she, never with I.

options.text: I am going to play football in the stadium.
options.feedback: Correct: I always goes with am in the going to structure.

options.text: I are going to play football in the stadium.
options.feedback: Incorrect: are goes with you/we/they, not with I.

options.text: I be going to play football in the stadium.
options.feedback: Incorrect: be alone is not conjugated; with I we need am.

questions.explanation: El verbo be debe concordar: I am, he/she is, you/we/they are. Con I, la forma correcta es am going to.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Sincelejo, Sucre, Laura says: "She ___ going to dance at the party". She needs am/is/are.

options.text: She am going to dance at the party.
options.feedback: Incorrect: am only goes with I.

options.text: She are going to dance at the party.
options.feedback: Incorrect: are goes with you/we/they, not with she.

options.text: She be going to dance at the party.
options.feedback: Incorrect: be must be conjugated; with she we need is.

options.text: She is going to dance at the party.
options.feedback: Correct: he/she/it always go with is in the going to structure.

questions.explanation: Con he, she e it se usa is: she is going to dance. La concordancia del verbo be es la clave de la estructura.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the message, what are they going to do on Sunday?
questions.context: Read the message from Valledupar, Cesar: "Hi! On Sunday we are going to visit the park. We are going to play football and eat ice cream. It is going to be fun!"

options.text: Visit the park, play football and eat ice cream.
options.feedback: Correct: the three going to verbs list exactly the Sunday plan.

options.text: Stay at home and watch television.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the message never mentions home or television.

options.text: Travel to another country by plane.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the plan is local, in the park, not a trip abroad.

options.text: Study mathematics all day.
options.feedback: Incorrect: there is no mention of studying or mathematics.

questions.explanation: Comprender planes futuros exige seguir los verbos con going to: visit, play y eat describen el domingo.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What are the parts of that future structure?
questions.context: In Quibdó, Chocó, a student wrote: "They are going to swim in the river". The teacher asks how the future is built.

options.text: Present verb + yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect: yesterday marks past, not future, and there is no going to.

options.text: Verb in past with -ed.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the -ed ending marks past, not a weekend plan.

options.text: Are (be for they) + going to + swim (main verb).
options.feedback: Correct: the structure has three parts: conjugated be, going to, and the base verb.

options.text: Going + to + river.
options.feedback: Incorrect: river is the place, not the main verb of the plan.

questions.explanation: Analizar la estructura muestra sus tres piezas: be conjugado (are), going to y el verbo en base (swim).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which plan sounds like a weekend activity and why?
questions.context: In Popayán, Cauca, two weekend plans compete: "We are going to clean the classroom" and "We are going to play in the park".

options.text: The first, because clean the classroom is typical weekend fun.
options.feedback: Incorrect: cleaning the classroom is a school duty, not weekend fun.

options.text: The second, because play in the park is a typical free-time activity with a place verb.
options.feedback: Correct: play is an activity verb and park is a weekend place; together they form a natural plan.

options.text: Both, because clean and play mean the same.
options.feedback: Incorrect: clean and play are different verbs with different meanings.

options.text: None, because going to cannot express fun.
options.feedback: Incorrect: going to can express any plan, including fun ones.

questions.explanation: El vocabulario distingue deberes (clean the classroom) de diversión (play in the park). Analizar verbo y lugar revela el plan más natural.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: How should the presentation be evaluated?
questions.context: In Yopal, Casanare, a student presents: "I is going to visit the library, they is going to play football and we am going to swim".

options.text: It is perfect because is and am agree with every subject.
options.feedback: Incorrect: is does not go with I or they, and am does not go with we.

options.text: It is perfect because going to never needs be.
options.feedback: Incorrect: going to always needs be conjugated before it.

options.text: Only the verbs visit, play and swim are wrong.
options.feedback: Incorrect: those main verbs are correct in base form; the errors are in be.

options.text: It has three errors in be: I requires am, they require are and we require are; the main verbs are correct.
options.feedback: Correct: evaluates each subject-be pair and keeps the base verbs visit, play and swim.

questions.explanation: Evaluar exige revisar cada pareja sujeto-be: I am, they are, we are. Los verbos principales van siempre en forma base después de going to.
questions.subject: ingles
